items.title: RBI Approves SBI Mutual Fund's Stake in South Indian Bank

items.summary: Gold held near $3,630 an ounce on Tuesday after surging Monday following Jensen Huang's surprise return as president and CEO of Nvidia Corp., the world's largest chipmaker. The rehiring occurred less than two weeks after Huang resigned amid a scandal, reigniting bets on artificial intelligence and propelling Wall Street to its best day since April 2025. Gold had partially retraced last week's near-9 per cent drop that took it to its lowest level in more than a year; the earlier decline was driven by an technology-stock rout prompting investors to sell bullion, alongside stubborn inflation and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary. Hebe Chen, senior market analyst at Vantage Global Prime, attributed gold's sharp rebound to Huang's return reigniting risk appetite across markets, while softer oil prices and easing longer-dated U.S. Treasury yields also supported the metal; however, she cautioned that it remains premature to call a bottom because these supportive forces have yet to prove they can sustain more than a short-lived relief rally. Investors still expect monetary policy to remain tight in coming months: Fed New York President John Williams said Monday that the central bank still has 'work to do' to tame sticky inflation, and markets are pricing in another interest-rate hike at the December meeting, which higher borrowing costs typically weigh on gold since it pays no interest. Elsewhere, Chinese gold imports surged to a record $209 billion so far this year amid an unprecedented buying spree that is helping keep a lid on China's trade surplus with partners like the European Union.
items.title: Gold Holds Gain After Nvidia Rehires Jensen Huang, Sparking AI Rally

items.summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt publicly endorsed the warning from Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang about the rapid rise of artificial intelligence, calling Wang's assessment 'correct.' The endorsement followed a detailed post shared by Wang on X (formerly Twitter), in which he warned that humanity may already be entering an era of superintelligence and cautioned that the coming year could prove decisive in determining whether ultra-powerful AI systems benefit people or spiral beyond human control. While acknowledging AI's ability to accelerate scientific and economic progress, Wang stressed that humans must remain actively involved in steering society rather than quietly handing it over to machines. Schmidt reshared Wang's note with praise for its extraordinary insight, noting he is among industry leaders who support AI while repeatedly warning about its dangers if humans fail to control it. He pointed to science as an area where AI could help, suggesting professors, graduate students, and postdoctoral researchers can work alongside supervised AI agents for problem-solving, but blamed technology companies for failing to highlight the technology's benefits—arguing that people are more likely to focus on negatives than positives. In his original post, Wang declared 'superintelligence is arriving,' citing recent breakthroughs showing machines quickly catching up to and surpassing human intellect in some areas. He pointed to reported proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as evidence of a dramatic shift, describing it as an intellectual feat highlighting what he termed an 'alien mind' that humans do not fully comprehend. Wang argued that solving elite mathematical problems demands more intellectual capacity than most everyday tasks handled by software engineers and other professionals, noting that shrinking practical roadblocks have made modern models highly effective across coding, cybersecurity, and other industries. He expects AI to become the primary driver of progress across nearly every field while questioning whether humanity can maintain control over unconstrained recursive self-improvement or a superintelligence 1,000 times smarter than people in every discipline.
items.title: Ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt Endorses Meta AI Chief's Superintelligence Warning

items.summary: On Monday, Anthropic announced the launch of Claude Ship, a tool designed to help developers ship code faster by reviewing changes, fixing problems, and deciding which ones can be added to the main code based on rules set by teams. The company said it is not intended to approve or merge code changes on its own; instead, it explains the changes it makes and how to undo them. Claude Ship has three parts: Code Review, which is already available, plus two new tools in beta testing—PR Steward and Claude Approvals. Code Review checks proposed code changes and flags problems. PR Steward helps resolve failed automated checks on a change, conflicts between code changes, and reviewer comments. Claude Approvals can approve routine changes automatically if team rules allow it, while sending riskier ones to a human for review. Anthropic said the tool is available from Monday on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for projects hosted on GitHub.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship Code-Review Tool

items.summary: The boards of SpaceX and Tesla have appointed five directors to special committees tasked with overseeing discussions on a potential merger between the two companies, according to The Financial Times reporting Tuesday citing people familiar with the matter. The committee includes two directors from SpaceX—Roelof Botha and Randy Glein—and three from Tesla: Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, and Jack Hartung. Musk had previously stated during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call last month that merging his AI, robotics, electric vehicle, and aerospace ambitions under a single corporate umbrella would be "a good idea," and confirmed the two companies had formed special committees of independent directors to explore a potential merger. The committees have hired financial advisers—Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs for SpaceX, and Evercore for Tesla—to prepare models that will help determine their negotiating positions in what could become an all-stock merger, per the report; the bankers are also assessing areas of overlap between the businesses and how a combined company could be structured.
items.title: SpaceX and Tesla Appoint Directors to Merger Committee

items.summary: Apple is preparing to release red versions of its entry-level speaker, the HomePod mini 2, and its high-end headphones, the AirPods Max 2. According to people familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified because the announcements are not public, Apple is gearing up for these launches as part of a revival of its longstanding Product(RED) partnership that raises money to fight AIDS while offering fresh colors during the holiday season.
items.title: Apple Revives Product(RED) Partnership with Red HomePod mini and AirPods Max

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has proposed draft guidelines that would give bank customers greater control over digital payments, with most measures set to take effect on 1 July 2027. Under the proposal, customers could switch payment channels such as internet or mobile banking on and off for specified periods and reactivate them after verification; new accounts' digital payment channels would start disabled and require explicit customer consent and verification before activation, with banks setting a transfer limit for the first 24 hours after activation. New debit, credit and prepaid cards would initially work only at domestic ATMs and shop terminals, while online, contactless and overseas use would begin disabled except for foreign-currency prepaid cards. Customers could set limits per transaction, recipient, day or across all digital channels—for example, a ₹20,000 daily limit on one recipient would cap transfers to that person even if the bank's standard limit is higher. A proposed 'stop switch' would block covered outgoing payments initiated by the customer, prevent new payment mandates and stop an account from being registered for UPI on a new app; incoming credits could continue while existing mandates, standing instructions, bank charges and loan instalments might still be processed, though banks could keep placing holds on funds. Customers could nominate a trusted adult to approve transfers above a chosen threshold within one hour of receiving the amount and recipient details, with no access to the account balance or authority to operate it; activation or changes would have a 24-hour cooling-off period, while UPI, merchant payments and existing recurring payments are exempt. The draft also broadens bank negligence in unauthorised transactions to cover failures to offer or enforce payment controls, verify customers, send alerts or act promptly on fraud reports, plus security failures and staff or contractor collusion, with refunds dependent on the circumstances of each case. Some verification, alert and fraud-reporting provisions are proposed for 1 January 2027; the draft covers public and private sector banks but exempts small finance banks, payments banks, regional rural banks and local area banks.
items.title: RBI Proposes 'Stop Switch' to Give Customers Greater Control Over Digital Payments

items.summary: Speaking at the Primary Dealers Association of India (PDAI) Seminar 2026 in Mumbai on Monday, RBI Deputy Governor Rohit Jain flagged concerns over declining demand for long-term government securities from banks, insurance companies and pension funds. He said increasing equity exposure among institutional investors has structurally weakened demand for long-term sovereign debt as these participants gradually shift toward equities. Banks remained the largest holders of government securities at nearly 35% of total holdings at the end of March 2026, followed by insurance companies and provident funds. Jain cautioned that rising bond yields could increase the financial burden on the exchequer, noting even a small yield increase can meaningfully impact interest costs while India's market remains heavily dependent on domestic institutional investors to absorb growing debt supply. He also highlighted geopolitical uncertainties as potential implications for borrowing costs and financial stability. To address these challenges, the RBI is encouraging primary dealers to strengthen market-making activities by providing two-way quotes for less frequently traded government securities to improve secondary-market liquidity and price discovery. Jain stressed that a coordinated approach requiring credible fiscal policies, effective debt management, predictable auctions and greater participation from long-term institutional investors would support sustainable borrowing and financial stability.
items.title: RBI Warns Of Mounting Interest Burden As Long-Term Bond Demand Squeezed

items.summary:
Google has dismissed reports of large-scale job cuts in its Cloud division in India as 'totally inaccurate', confirming that approximately 30 roles were eliminated last week as part of a business restructuring exercise. In a post on X on Monday, the official Google Cloud India account described claims of widespread layoffs as false, stating the changes were limited to a small organizational adjustment linked to a reprioritization of work: 'These rumors are totally inaccurate. Last week, Google Cloud made a small organizational change in India, and approximately 30 roles were eliminated as part of a re-prioritization of work.' The company shared the same clarification in response to several posts discussing possible layoffs.

Speculation about job cuts had been circulating on X for two days before Google's response. The discussion reportedly began on the anonymous professional networking platform Blind, where a user claiming to be a Bengaluru-based Google employee alleged that staff members in India were facing sudden job cuts, including demands to resign or risk being fired. The post also claimed some employees were given only 24 hours to make a decision with one month's severance pay, and further alleged performance improvement plans were used to prevent internal transfers while raising the possibility of additional voluntary exit programs or layoffs in January; these claims were not independently established.

The Blind post was subsequently shared on X, prompting several users to ask whether Google planned major job cuts in India. User Venkatesh Alla asked about reports of 'Huge layoffs at Google India,' and Google Cloud India's official account responded that the reports were inaccurate and only around 30 positions had been affected. Some people identifying themselves as Google employees also disputed wider layoff claims; X user Bhavya Khandelwal, a software engineer, wrote 'Fake hysteria - I'm in the org,' while Akash Basudevan, a senior machine learning engineer, said 'I don't see it anywhere yet.'

Google has carried out multiple rounds of workforce reductions since January 2023 as part of efforts to control costs, simplify its organizational structure, and shift resources toward priority areas, particularly artificial intelligence. In January 2023, the company announced plans to eliminate around 12,000 jobs worldwide, representing approximately 6% of its workforce (per candidate readings). Smaller cuts continued in 2024; in January that year, Google confirmed job reductions affecting several hundred employees across its hardware, central engineering, and Google Assistant teams. More recently, Google offered voluntary buyout and exit packages to selected employees in five countries: Canada, France, Germany, Japan, and Switzerland, as it managed costs amid substantial spending on artificial intelligence.
items.title: Google Rejects Mass Layoff Claims in India, Confirms Elimination of ~30 Roles

items.summary:
A joint India-US investigation into a cross-border drug trafficking network has resulted in the arrest of six Indians, according to news agency PTI. Investigators are tracing an alleged supply chain involving thousands of parcels, online orders, and cryptocurrency payments used to ship opioid medicines from India to customers in the United States. The operation reportedly distributed medications including Xanax (Alprazolam), Ativan, Tramadol, Valium (Diazepam), and Ambien.

Among those arrested is T Manoj, 27, a man from Telangana who was deported from the US in January 2024 for allegedly trading regulated drugs. He holds a BTech degree in Computer Science and had been pursuing a master's degree while investigators examine his links in both countries. A Muttalib, 28, from Kolkata, also faces charges; he holds an engineering degree and was engaged in cloth manufacturing and the dairy business.
items.title: Six Indians Arrested in Joint India-US Drug Trafficking Investigation

items.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin, and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal formally announced a renewed alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party and SAD ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections at BJP headquarters in New Delhi on Tuesday. The two parties agreed to contest all 117 Assembly seats together, with the SAD set to receive the chief minister's post as part of the arrangement (Union Times of India). Shah said the alliance would be fought jointly and confirmed that the Akali Dal would rejoin the NDA from that day, calling it a return on Guru Purab for one of their oldest allies. He added that Prime Minister Modi had spoken with Badal about expanding the NDA, describing the tie-up as symbolizing brotherhood between the two parties (Union Times of India). HM Shah outlined the alliance's priorities, identifying eradication of drugs and corruption and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab as key goals while announcing a deadline for making the state drug-free. The BJP and SAD had ended their alliance in 2020 after the Akali Dal withdrew from the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed; the parties then contested the 2022 Assembly elections separately (Union Times of India). Their electoral fortunes declined afterward: in 2017 the SAD won 15 seats and the BJP three, while in 2022 the SAD secured three seats and the BJP two, with AAP winning 92 seats (Union Times of India). Aam Aadmi Party national convenor Arvind Kejriwal accused the parties of uniting for power, arguing that political alliances form and break for convenience rather than development. He said his alliance is with Punjab's mothers and daughters, SC community, farmers, and traders, noting Bhagwant Mann has worked to repair damage inflicted on Punjab over 70-75 years (Union Times of India). AAP leader Jarnail Singh argued that 'zero plus zero will always remain zero,' asserting the Akali Dal and BJP have no future in Punjab because people rejected both parties. He cited more than 700 farmers who lost their lives during protests against the Centre's farm laws and referred to the sacrilege of Guru Granth Sahib during the Akali Dal government (Union Times of India). Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh termed the alliance 'directionless,' alleging it was driven by greed for power with no development agenda or roadmap, asserting neither party could form the next government. He asked Badal why he quit the NDA in 2020 and told PTI that both parties joined hands only to capture power (Union Times of India). Earlier, Amarinder Singh Raja Warring had criticized the proposed alliance before its formal announcement, accusing SAD leaders Sukhbir Singh Badal and Harsimrat Kaur Badal of misleading voters over their political ties with BJP. He questioned why the two parties split in 2020 and alleged that Akali Dal initially supported the three farm laws before changing position following farmers' protests (Union Times of India). The article notes that AAP, Congress reacted to the announcement on Tuesday.
items.title: BJP and SAD Announce Renewed Alliance for 2027 Punjab Elections

items.summary: A November 2025 study published in the Journal of Biogeography traced the genetic history of Korthalsia laciniosa, a climbing palm (rattan) found across the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, revealing distinct evolutionary histories on either side of the Ten Degree Channel. Researchers collected leaf samples from 258 individual plants across 13 populations in Andaman, Havelock, Little Andaman, Great Nicobar, and North Nicobar islands, then examined microsatellite DNA sequences to estimate genetic diversity and relatedness patterns (Journal of Biogeography). The analysis found a deep genetic divide between the two island groups with low interbreeding levels, indicating separate ancestral origins. Sarath Paremmal, the study's lead author who worked on these palms during his Ph.D. at the Kerala Forest Research Institute, stated that Andaman populations likely derive from Indo-Burmese regions like Myanmar while Nicobar regions have a stronger evolutionary connection with Sumatra; however, he noted the team could not obtain samples from Sumatra or Myanmar to test this theory specifically for the palm (Journal of Biogeography). The Nicobar populations showed relatively low genetic diversity within populations and variants largely restricted to that island group, indicating they maintained a distinct genetic identity. Little Andaman was genetically distinct from other Andaman populations, possibly due to geographic distance, with genetic differences generally increasing with geographic distances in middle and southern islands (Journal of Biogeography). The study also examined the last glacial maximum period approximately 21,000 years ago when global sea levels fell as far as 120 metres. Paremmal said suitable habitat during this period was concentrated in the southern Andaman Islands including Little Andaman, and demographic models suggest populations were restricted to southern Andaman then expanded northwards as warming set in and sea levels rose after the ice age (Journal of Biogeography). The researchers noted that although this model is not a true reconstruction of where ancestral populations existed, it was the best-supported scenario among several tested. G. Ravikanth, a senior fellow at ATREE Academy in Bengaluru who is not associated with the study, stated that South Andaman holds rattan diversity that cannot be rebuilt elsewhere and emphasized non-substitutability for Great Nicobar's genetically distinct cluster containing 14 private alleles at one sampled site; he added three conservation actions including managing Nicobar and Andaman stocks as separate units, treating Little Andaman provisionally as its own unit, securing South Andaman evergreen forest patches, mapping populations systematically, collecting ex-situ material per sub-population, and monitoring these groups (Journal of Biogeography).
items.title: Genetic Analysis Reveals Deep Evolutionary Divide in Andaman and Nicobar Climbing Palm

items.summary: According to the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), private-sector project announcements surged 58.5% year-on-year to ₹26.6 trillion in the first half of fiscal year 2027 (H1 FY27, April–September 2026), signaling a sharp expansion in India's investment pipeline with manufacturing, electricity, and technology-related infrastructure as key drivers. The figures come from CII's second edition of its Private Investment Barometer.
items.title: CII: Private Project Announcements Jumped 58.5% to ₹26.6 Trillion in H1 FY27

items.summary:
The Kerala government has constituted a three-member expert committee to assess air quality trends in Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram, Chief Minister V D Satheesan announced on Tuesday. The decision follows concerns over rising pollution levels and discrepancies in Air Quality Index (AQI) readings reported by different agencies for the two cities, according to a statement from the state's Chief Medical Officer.

The panel will be chaired by the head of the Kerala State Pollution Control Board, with Suresh Ramasubramanian Iyer—Senior Fellow and Area Convener at the Centre for Air Quality Research, The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI), New Delhi—and Dr George K Varghese, Professor in the Department of Civil Engineering at NIT Calicut serving as other members.

The committee will examine five years of air quality changes in both cities, including variations attributable to climatic and geographical factors. It will investigate discrepancies between AQI figures reported by different agencies and monitoring systems, recommend an authoritative standard for reporting air quality data statewide, assess the adequacy and reliability of existing monitoring infrastructure, and identify major pollution sources such as vehicular emissions, construction activities, road dust, waste burning, industrial operations, and port and airport activity.

Based on its findings, the panel will propose short-term and long-term measures to curb pollution. It is also expected to recommend a transparent public communication mechanism that strengthens the monitoring network, makes real-time AQI data accessible to citizens, and issues health advisories. Chief Minister Satheesan has directed the committee to submit its report within two weeks.
items.title: Kerala Forms Expert Panel to Assess Air Quality in Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram

items.summary: On November 22, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt. Ltd under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, over a packaged drinking water sample it declared unsafe. A sanction allows the regulator to take a case to court but is not a finding of guilt; Bisleri maintains its water is safe.
items.title: FSSAI Sanctions Prosecution of Bisleri Over Unsafe Packaged Water Sample

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party and Shiromani Akali Dal have renewed their alliance after six years to contest the upcoming Punjab assembly elections jointly, endorsing Sukhbir Singh Badal as their chief ministerial candidate. The two parties celebrated the renewal of their partnership with sweets and fireworks in Chandigarh. Their joint campaign will begin with a rally in Moga on Parkash Singh Badal's birth anniversary, focusing on issues such as drug eradication, law and order, and corruption. While Akali Dal remains the senior partner in the alliance, BJP plans to contest over 45 seats across Punjab assembly constituencies. The renewal of this partnership aims to reshape the political landscape ahead of elections through a triangular contest involving Congress and Aam Aadmi Party. According to experts analyzing the situation, the BJP-Akali Dal alliance is expected to influence voter trends and party leadership dynamics in the state.
items.title: BJP and Akali Dal Renew Alliance with Badal as CM Candidate for Punjab Elections

items.summary: An FSSAI-related laboratory examination found a Bisleri water sample contained bromate levels exceeding prescribed limits, and a referral food laboratory also detected polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), declaring the sample unsafe. Both chemicals are linked to cancer and raise serious health concerns. The source states that for years millions of Indians have trusted Bisleri as a provider of safe bottled drinking water, but this test has raised questions about packaged water safety. Bisleri denied the allegations. A video explainer covering these findings is available through the referenced watch item.
items.title: FSSAI Declares Bisleri Water Sample Unsafe Over Bromate, PAHs

items.summary: The Congress questioned Union Health Minister J P Nadda on Tuesday over a Union Health Ministry report flagging high anaemia prevalence in Gujarat during 2023-25, according to news agency Press Trust of India. The report, titled 'Anaemia and Micronutrient Deficiencies Across the Life Course in India' and released by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, was cited by Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh on X. It found anaemia affected 61.4 per cent of adolescent girls aged 10 to 19, 63.8 per cent of adult women aged 20 to 59, and 66.2 per cent of women of reproductive age aged 15 to 49 in Gujarat during the period. Ramesh said only Chhattisgarh fared worse, while Kerala's figures were 21.4 per cent for adolescent girls, 28 per cent for adult women, and 29.1 per cent for women of reproductive age; he described these as high but far below Gujarat's levels, which have been promoted by the prime minister as a model state. The report also found Gujarat had the highest anaemia prevalence among children aged 12 to 59 months at 56.5 per cent, while Kerala recorded the lowest at 14.5 per cent. Ramesh asked whether Nadda would 'survive' the release of what he called a damning report.
items.title: Congress Questions JP Nadda Over Gujarat's High Anaemia Burden

items.summary: Agriculture Minister T Siddique said on Tuesday that Kerala will implement the 'Nutri Tuber Keralam' scheme to expand tuber crop cultivation, promote food self-sufficiency and improve public health. The initiative aims to boost food production by encouraging tuber crops as intercrops and promoting nutritious eating habits, he said while inaugurating State Tuber Crops Day celebrations at the ICAR-Central Tuber Crops Research Institute in Sreekariyam on Tuesday. Siddique said the scheme would be implemented in coordination with Krishi Bhavans, tribal communities and farmers. He added that changing food habits and excessive use of pesticides in vegetables were having serious repercussions on public health, noting that pesticide residues in food contributed to a rise in cancer, kidney ailments and lifestyle diseases, forcing people in Kerala to spend heavily on healthcare. The minister called upon people to embrace the concept of 'My food, my responsibility' and take up cultivation of tuber crops.
items.title: Kerala to promote tuber crops as intercrops under new scheme

items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi discussed her internal conflict over accepting the prime minister's post after the Congress-led UPA won the 2004 Lok Sabha elections, during a video conversation with her son Rahul Gandhi and daughter Priyanka Gandhi Vadra about her memoir 'Belonging.' The discussion was shared on their social media handles. Sonia said she felt a "pull of power" when deciding whether to take up the office, describing how she worried that accepting it would betray Congress workers who had rallied across the country during the election campaign and voted for the party throughout. She acknowledged wondering how she could let those workers down by declining the premiership, adding that this was something she wanted to believe in order to justify saying yes. Sonia said the experience taught her a lesson about power: "once you are there and you have it (power), you may find many excuses to keep it," noting she is examining this psychological tendency within herself. Rahul Gandhi recalled discussing the decision process, stating that while his mother was uncertain about taking up the premiership, seven people were in line for the post, with Manmohan Singh being "the best possible PM" due to his qualities and capabilities, contrasting him with six or seven others who he described as dreamers unable to hold the office. Rahul said there was joy in the room when Sonia declined the position. After deliberation, Sonia Gandhi chose not to accept the prime minister's post and selected Manmohan Singh for the role. The three also discussed childhood memories, political turmoil, and alleged lapses in security before former PM Rajiv Gandhi's assassination; Priyanka recalled how Sonia had grown more vigilant after Rajiv entered politics and following his 1991 death. Sonia shared the video on X, writing that she created 'Belonging' from her own memories while Rahul and Priyanka added theirs.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Reflects on 'Pull of Power' in 2004 PM Decision

Ltd., describes the founder's journey behind his online platform that lets citizens securely and on-the-go access their health records.
items.title: Former Merrill Lynch banker Harsh Parikh cofounds health-records startup DRiefcase

items.summary: A study published in the journal Sleep, titled 'Failing to plan: Bedtime planning, bedtime procrastination, and objective sleep in university students,' examined how delaying sleep despite feeling tired affects rest. Researchers Zhenghao Pu, Alyssa S C Ng, Sooyeon Suh, Michael W L Chee and Stijn A A Massar tracked 119 full-time National University of Singapore students over two to four weeks using a smartphone app for bedtime intentions and Oura rings for objective sleep data.
items.title: Study Links Bedtime Procrastination to Poor Sleep and Self-Regulation

items.summary: Aravind Sampath and SSS Kumar of IIM Kozhikode argue that Indian capital markets require stable tax policy rather than ad-hoc adjustments. They characterize the market as having faced at least four distinct tax structures—on dividends, fixed income, short-term capital gains (STCG), and long-term capital gains (LTCG)—plus Securities Transaction Tax (STT). LTCG has undergone sharp ideological reversals over roughly two and a half decades: it was abolished in 2004 under Section 10(38) with STT introduced as an alternative, reintroduced at 10% on gains exceeding ₹ 1 lakh via Section 112A in 2018 while keeping STT intact, then raised to 12.5% with the threshold increased to ₹ 1.25 lakh in the 2024 budget session. The authors note that grandfathering provisions from 2018 protect historical gains but diminish returns on subsequent investment lifecycle gains under the new tax liability. They distinguish STCG, borne by short-term and speculative traders who typically hold positions of a few months at best through frequent churning, from LTCG, carried by patient long-horizon investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth managers, and systematic investment plan (SIP) participants holding for multi-year or decade periods. The authors contend that mid-cycle changes to LTCG cause policy-induced portfolio underperformance on top of existing global macro uncertainties, while greater structural benefits come from institutionalizing a multi-decadal framework with transparent recalibration tied to metrics like market capitalization or the market cap-to-GDP ratio.
items.title: LTCG Debate: Why Markets Need Tax Stability, Not Ad-Hoc Fixes

items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday denied bail to Shubham Tyagi, an operator of a paying guest accommodation that collapsed on September 6 at the five-storey Satya Niketan building, killing seven people. An additional sessions judge at Patiala House Courts said Tyagi could have foreseen the danger posed by construction work but had prioritised financial benefits over the safety of students and labourers, adding that those responsible for losing lives are not entitled to bail discretion and such incidents must be handled with an iron hand. The building was reportedly around 50 years old, and police said owners knew it could not bear four additional floors yet leased it out as a paying guest accommodation; Tyagi and co-accused Sudhanshu Lovenish Kumar had rented the property to operate Hostel Daze. The court noted that the accused failed to verify structural safety or take adequate precautions despite construction work, and observed that one injured person and other students complained about illegal basement construction around 10 to 12 days before the collapse but were threatened with eviction while work continued. Tyagi's lawyer argued he was wrongly implicated because he rented only the second and third floors without permission for structural changes, contending the basement and ground floor were under owner control and that a shop on the ground floor had construction allegedly carried out by another tenant; the court rejected these arguments, observing that Tyagi controlled the property after executing the rent agreement and was duty-bound to get it vacated until work completed. The report was filed based on Live Law reporting.
items.title: Delhi Court Denies Bail to Operator in Satya Niketan Building Collapse Case
